topic.title: Internationalization
topic.shortdesc: Language support, right-to-left text, locale-aware typography, and CJK considerations.

body.p: The internationalizationDITA2ePub plugin supports content in multiple languages with features that go beyond simple text translation. The plugin adapts its output based on the xml:lang attribute in your DITA source, automatically adjusting text direction, quotation marks, and generated labels.

section.title: Language Detection
section.p: The publication language is determined from three sources, in order:

ol.li: The xml:lang attribute on the root bookmap or map element

section.p: The language affects the dc:language metadata in the OPF, the xml:lang attribute on all generated XHTML files, and the text direction of the publication.

section.title: Right-to-Left Support
section.p: right-to-leftRTLWhen the publication language is Arabic (ar), Hebrew (he), Farsi (fa), or Urdu (ur), the plugin automatically:

ul.li: Sets dir="rtl" on all generated HTML elements
Configures page-progression-direction="rtl" in the OPF spine

section.p: Bidirectional text within a predominantly LTR or RTL document is handled by the Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm, which is implemented by all modern reading systems.

section.title: Localized Labels
section.p: The plugin generates localized labelshuman-readable labels for notes, navigation headings, and structural elements. These labels are localized for twelve languages:

row.entry: 注記, 警告, ヒント
注意, 警告, 提示

section.title: Locale-Aware Quotation Marks
section.p: When quotation markslocale-awareepub.locale.quotes=yes, the plugin transforms straight quotation marks in the output to the typographically correct marks for each language:

section.title: CJK Considerations
section.p: CJKdrop capsChinese, Japanese, and Korean text has specific typographic requirements. The plugin automatically suppresses drop caps for CJK languages, since the decorative initial-letter effect does not work well with ideographic characters.
